Definition: Integration of farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations, extension services data
Comments: No evidence of farmer registries or agricultural input system integration with government data exchange.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: World Bank Chad Digital Transformation Project appraisal document (2024) and the accompanying Digital Economy Diagnostic confirm Chad has no operational government-wide interoperability framework: existing back-office systems (SIGFiP, eTax, ASYCUDA) are siloed by ministry, and there are no end-user-facing G2B/G2P digital services. No agriculture-specific digitisation programme with a data-exchange linkage was found in further searches. The original 0 (Unknown) understated the evidence available; revised to 1 (Not integrated) because the absence of both a national data exchange and of agriculture-specific integration is now documented rather than merely unknown.
revised_comments: Chad has not established a functioning cross-government data exchange, so farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations and extension services data are not linked to any such platform. Government digital systems in Chad remain siloed by ministry, with no interoperability framework in place to connect agricultural-sector data to other administrative systems.

Definition: Integration of learner records, academic credentials, enrollment data, and scholarship/bursary systems
Comments: No evidence of education system integration with government data exchange. Digital skills gaps noted across public servants.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) rested on a generic World Bank digital-transformation project document with no education-specific evidence. Further search identifies a functioning, sector-specific Education Management Information System (EMIS, established 2014) and a UNESCO/Global Partnership for Education review (2021–2023) that explicitly notes the absence of unique school-level codification linking EMIS to other administrative platforms, and weak coordination of data with other ministries and partners. This supports 'Not integrated' (1) rather than 'Unknown' (0): a digitised, standalone education data system exists but is not linked to the broader government data exchange.
revised_comments: Chad's Education Management Information System (EMIS), in place since 2014 under the Ministry of National Education and Civic Promotion, collects school-level data and publishes annual statistical yearbooks, but a UNESCO-led audit finds no unique school codification linking EMIS to other administrative platforms, and coordination of education data across ministries and partners remains weak. Learner records, academic credentials and enrolment data are therefore not integrated with a cross-government data exchange.

Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: Chad went through transition government (2021-2024); senatorial elections held February 2025. No documented integration with digital exchange.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original source was a general World Bank PAD with no electoral-specific content. Searches on Chad's electoral commission (CENI) and its biometric voter-roll update for the December 2023 constitutional referendum confirm a standalone electoral register system, with no documented data-sharing link to ANATS's national biometric population register or to any wider government data exchange. Revised from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (Not integrated) since the separateness of the systems is now evidenced rather than simply unknown.
revised_comments: Chad's electoral register is compiled and maintained independently by the National Independent Electoral Commission (CENI) using its own biometric voter-registration system, most recently updated for the December 2023 constitutional referendum. There is no evidence that this biometric electoral roll is linked to the national biometric population register (ANATS) or to any wider government data exchange; voter registration and civil identity management remain separate processes.

Comments: No evidence of employment services integration with government data exchange.

revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) rested on a generic World Bank document with no employment-specific content. Further research identifies Chad's National Employment Promotion Office (ONAPE) operating its own online job-seeker platform and a dedicated service window launched in June 2025, but finds no evidence that this feeds into or draws on a wider government data exchange linking employment records with unemployment insurance, social protection or other administrative databases. Revised to 1 (Not integrated) since a digitised but siloed employment registry is now documented.
revised_comments: Chad's National Employment Promotion Office (ONAPE) operates its own online platform (onape.td) enabling job seekers to register, maintain CVs and receive vacancy alerts, and launched a dedicated 'Guichet de la Recherche Emploi Salarié' service window in June 2025. This is a standalone sectoral system; there is no evidence that it draws on or feeds into a wider government data exchange linking employment records with unemployment insurance, social protection or other administrative databases.

Definition: Integration of court records, case management systems, correctional services data, legal aid information
Comments: No evidence of court/justice system integration with government data exchange.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) rested on a generic World Bank PID. Further searches found a genuine, dated development: Chad's Ministry of Justice, with UNDP support, launched a pilot 'e-Justice' case-management and information-exchange platform in N'Djamena in October 2025, with administrator training continuing into February 2026 ahead of a planned national roll-out. This is a materially different picture from 'no evidence of digitisation', but it remains unclear whether this internal justice-sector platform constitutes 'integration' with the broader cross-government data exchange (the variable's stated scope) as opposed to sector-internal case management digitisation. Provisionally scored 1 (Not integrated with the cross-government exchange) pending clarification; flagged for human review because a higher score (2 or 3) may be warranted if the variable is meant to capture the justice sector's own digitisation progress.
revised_comments: Chad's Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, supported by the UN Development Programme, launched a pilot e-Justice case-management and information-exchange platform in N'Djamena in October 2025, with administrator training continuing into February 2026 ahead of a planned national roll-out. The platform links justiciables, lawyers and judicial personnel within the justice sector, but there is no evidence that it yet exchanges data with other government systems, such as civil registration or digital identity, via a cross-government data exchange.

Definition: Integration of passport issuance and immigration control data into the exchange platform
Comments: No evidence of passport/immigration data integration with government data exchange. Liber Technologies developed e-visa system for Chad (mentioned as a separate project in the Cameroon-Liber partnership context) but no integration with broader exchange.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The original source was almost entirely about Cameroon's CRVS reforms and mentioned Chad only in passing regarding an unrelated e-visa vendor; it does not support this variable and is discarded. A dedicated search found a March 2026 report describing a signed interoperability agreement between the National Agency for Secure Documents (ANATS, which issues passports and IDs via its SIGPTS biometric register) and the Ministry of Finance, intended to extend to other ministries as the country's 'single source of truth' for identity verification. This is concrete and recent, warranting an upgrade from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Under development). However, it rests on a single trade-press source describing one bilateral agreement rather than a documented multi-agency rollout, so it is flagged for human review rather than asserted with full confidence.
revised_comments: Chad's passports and national identity documents are issued through ANATS's Integrated Population and Secure Documents Management System (SIGPTS), a single biometric population register operational since 2020. In March 2026, ANATS signed an interoperability agreement with the Ministry of Finance to enable real-time data sharing from this biometric registry, with the stated aim of connecting other government ministries and agencies to it as the country's single source of truth for identity verification. This represents an early stage of integrating passport and immigration identity data into a broader government data exchange, with one ministry (Finance) confirmed as connected so far.

Definition: Integration of statistics, census data, administrative data for planning, M&E, and evidence-based policymaking
Comments: No evidence of national statistics/census data integrated with government interoperability platform.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) rested on a generic World Bank PID. A World Bank statistical capacity-building project appraisal identifies long-standing, explicit gaps in harmonising and integrating administrative statistics across sectors (education, employment, health, justice, civil registration, business, telecoms), and the 2024 Digital Transformation Project appraisal confirms these silos persist. This supports revision to 1 (Not integrated) rather than 0 (Unknown), since the absence of integration is now documented rather than simply unresearched.
revised_comments: Chad's National Institute of Statistics, Economic and Demographic Studies (INSEED) collects and disseminates national surveys and census data through its own data portal, but administrative data held by sector ministries (education, health, employment, justice, civil registration, business, telecommunications) remains poorly harmonised and is not integrated into a shared government data exchange for planning and monitoring purposes. Chad's government systems remain siloed by ministry, with no whole-of-government interoperability framework linking statistical, administrative and planning data.

revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) is revised to 1 (No) given consistent, authoritative evidence (World Bank Chad Digital Transformation Project appraisal document, 2024, and the accompanying Digital Economy Diagnostic) that Chad has no operating cross-government data exchange or interoperability platform on which AI/analytics capabilities could run. revised_comments: There is no evidence of artificial intelligence or advanced analytics being used within any Chadian government data exchange or interoperability system. Chad's digital government infrastructure remains at a nascent, siloed stage, with basic interoperability between ministries not yet achieved, so no data-quality, fraud-detection or predictive-analytics applications have been identified.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: No public dashboard or transparency reporting on data exchange operations. Back-office systems (SIGFiP, eTax, ASYCUDA) are internal systems with no public visibility. Chad scored 0.1785 on EGDI 2024 (189/193).
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: Confirmed: the score of 1 is supported. The cited Ecofin Agency article (December 2025) does not itself discuss transparency but corroborates Chad's low 2024 UN E-Government Development Index ranking (189th of 193, EGDI 0.1785); the World Bank Chad Digital Transformation Project appraisal document (2024) and Digital Economy Diagnostic more directly confirm that Chad's back-office systems (SIGFiP, eTax, ASYCUDA) are internal to individual ministries, siloed, and not publicly disclosed, with no end-user-facing digital services. The blank Value Name should read 'None' per the variable's scale — a cosmetic labelling gap, not a scoring error; no change to Value Code is needed.
revised_comments: There is no public dashboard, published data-sharing agreement, or annual reporting on the operations and governance of any government data exchange in Chad. Existing back-office systems — the Integrated Public Finance Management System (SIGFiP), the eTax application, and ASYCUDA World for customs — are internal to individual ministries and are not disclosed to the public. Chad ranks 189th of 193 countries on the UN's 2024 E-Government Development Index (EGDI 0.1785), reflecting the very early stage of its digital government transparency and reporting practices.
